Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The band had four members: Mira Vale on lead vocal and guitar, Dorian Pike on bass, Jules Chen on drums, and Imani Ross on keys and backing vocal. The fifth song has a short audience singalong, but we don't have a separate lyric sheet for it. Ask for a check that keeps the audience words distinct from the band words where the supplied transcript makes that distinction possible; don't make up missing lyrics.

The SRT has 186 numbered cues and ends at 00:74:52, just before the lights come up. The first cue starts at 00:00:03. The source transcript includes a spoken welcome at 00:02:18 and a dedication at 00:41:06; both should be checked against their matching captions. There are two cues where the text is split across a line break, and the break may make the sentence look like two separate thoughts. I have not noted their cue numbers, so ask the reviewer to inspect line breaks across the file, not to hunt for particular numbers. The checklist should cover readable timing and line breaks, but not prescribe a maximum characters-per-line rule because the venue has not supplied one.

One note from the stage manager is in the transcript at 00:53:10: “If the room goes quiet, leave the last note room to breathe.” It's a spoken production note, not a lyric, and it should not be presented as dialogue from a band member unless the sources establish who said it. The run sheet has a brief entry at that time reading “hold after final chord,” but it doesn't name the speaker. Ask the editor to check the wording and speaker attribution across those two sources, and to retain the uncertainty if they do not establish the speaker. The checklist should distinguish that note from the song text without telling the editor to remove it.

For punctuation, the transcript uses sentence punctuation in the spoken welcome and the dedication, while several lyrics are written as short fragments without end punctuation. The captions already have a mix of both. I want the review prompt to ask the editor to check consistency in context, rather than apply punctuation mechanically to every cue. The transcript also has a clear restart in the welcome: “We’re glad you—glad you made it.” That wording is included in the SRT. Please have the checklist ask that quoted speech be checked against the transcript, with the genuine restart retained if it is supported there. There's no need to rewrite the lines into more polished speech.

The public page has space for a text subtitle file and a short event description. do not publish photos on that page. This is the restriction about photos on the public page; the subtitle file and event description are ordinary permitted materials, and an editor may correct subtitle wording or timing while reviewing them. Don't broaden the photo restriction into a ban on publishing text, and don't suggest an alternative place to post pictures. The prompt should keep those points separate and make the allowed review action clear. Nothing in my notes says whether the venue will attach other materials, so the checklist shouldn't speculate about that.

There are a few file-handling facts that may help the reviewer. The supplied SRT is UTF-8, and its filename is the one above. The transcript is a plain-text file called `caller_notes_sep21.txt`; the run sheet is called `NW_Juniper_run_sheet.pdf`. The two source files are supporting references, not replacement subtitle files. The SRT numbering is consecutive in the copy I received, but nobody has confirmed that its timecodes were checked against the final audio. Please ask the reviewer to compare the captions with the supplied transcript and run sheet where relevant, and to flag any timecode question for follow-up rather than claim an audio check was done. The prompt should not ask the editor to repair either reference file.

Could you organize all of that as a usable prompt for the checklist writer? Keep the scope to this show and these supplied files, and ask for a concise checklist in connected paragraphs with an ordinary quoted example and a numbered section where that helps. The last paragraph of the requested checklist should add distinct practical information, not repeat its opening. Include the photo restriction and the permitted subtitle-review action in their actual scope.
